title: Evidence uncertainty and decision guarantees in investment research
markdown:
## 1 Where existing methods leave the decision unresolved [SHAP](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.07874)'s local accuracy property decomposes a given model prediction into additive feature contributions, while conditional Shapley methods address feature dependence and Rashomon-set methods examine explanation stability across near-optimal models (*[SHAP](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.07874); [Aas et al.](https://arxiv.org/html/1903.10464v3); [Marx et al.](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v206/marx23a.html)*). However, **these explainability methods impose zero requirement that the underlying corporate input facts $`x`$ be true**. In institutional investment diligence—where self-reported disclosures may contain AI-polished greenwashing—a further mathematical layer is required to determine *which factual correction to the evidence could flip the current investment decision*. For a linear scoring model under a fixed marginal background $`Q`$, the [SHAP](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.07874) attribution assigned to feature $`j`$ is $`\phi_j = \beta_j(x_j - E_Q X_j)`$. Suppose feature $`j`$ carries an unresolved factual or greenwashing uncertainty bounded by $`|\delta_j| \le d_j`$. Its true sensitivity to factual verification is $`|\beta_j|d_j`$, and over a box of admissible evidence errors, the exact worst-case swing in the company's score is: $$ \sup_{|\delta_j| \le d_j} |f(x + \delta) - f(x)| = \sum_j |\beta_j| d_j $$ The triangle inequality gives the upper bound, which is attained by choosing the endpoint of each error interval so that all perturbations push the score in the same direction. This identity exposes a fundamental flaw in standard XAI-driven diligence: • A core financial metric with a massive [SHAP](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.07874) bar $`|\phi_j|`$ may come from audited statutory filings that have already been thoroughly verified ($`d_j \approx 0`$); re-auditing it wastes diligence budget. • Conversely, a self-reported ESG or operational metric whose current claimed value sits near the sector average ($`x_j \approx E_Q X_j \implies \phi_j \approx 0`$) appears completely unimportant on a [SHAP](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.07874) chart, yet may harbor substantial unresolved greenwashing error ($`d_j \gg 0`$) capable of reversing the deal ranking! Naive bootstrap resampling of existing records fails for a parallel reason: it cannot detect a shared reporting or AI-marketing bias. Suppose $`n`$ reported observations satisfy $`X_i = \mu + b + \varepsilon_i`$, where $`\varepsilon_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2)`$ are independent random errors and $`b \neq 0`$ is an unmodeled systemic bias shared across records (such as sector-wide self-reporting inflation or coordinated AI-PR sentiment manipulation). A conventional nominal 95% normal confidence interval centered on the sample mean $`\bar{X}`$ covers the true fundamental parameter $`\mu`$ with probability: $$ \Pr\left\{ \mu \in \left[ \bar{X} - z\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}}, \ \bar{X} + z\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}} \right] \right\} = \Phi\left( z - \frac{b\sqrt{n}}{\sigma} \right) - \Phi\left( -z - \frac{b\sqrt{n}}{\sigma} \right) \longrightarrow 0 \quad (\text{as } n \to \infty) $$ where $`z = \Phi^{-1}(0.975) \approx 1.96`$. **Collecting more biased documents ($`n \to \infty`$) shrinks random variance while driving true confidence coverage to zero!** A bootstrap that resamples the same biased disclosures has no statistical leverage to identify $`b`$. Active evidence verification must therefore bound input uncertainty before stability analysis can provide valid decision guarantees. ## 2 Joint uncertainty over models and evidence To evaluate whether an ESG or investment ranking is genuinely trustworthy, our engine represents **model-selection multiplicity** and **unresolved evidence uncertainty** jointly. Fix the prediction target, input definitions, and output scale. Consider $`M`$ candidate scoring models $`\mathcal{F}_0`$ specified before examining an independent validation set of size $`n`$ with loss bounded in $`[0, 1]`$. For failure probability $`\alpha \in (0, 1)`$, Hoeffding's inequality and a union bound guarantee: $$ \Pr\left\{ \max_{f \in \mathcal{F}_0} |\hat{L}_n(f) - L(f)| \le t_n \right\} \ge 1 - \alpha, \qquad t_n = \sqrt{\frac{\log(2M / \alpha)}{2n}} $$ Let $`f^*`$ minimize true population loss within $`\mathcal{F}_0`$, and retain the empirical **Rashomon set** of all near-optimal models within $`2t_n`$ of the empirical validation minimum: $$ \mathcal{F}_\alpha = \left\{ f \in \mathcal{F}_0 : \hat{L}_n(f) \le \min_{g \in \mathcal{F}_0} \hat{L}_n(g) + 2t_n \right\} $$ On the simultaneous concentration event, $`\hat{L}_n(f^*) \le L(f^*) + t_n \le \min_g \hat{L}_n(g) + 2t_n`$, guaranteeing $`f^* \in \mathcal{F}_\alpha`$ while every retained model has population excess loss at most $`4t_n`$ (*[Marx et al.](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v206/marx23a.html)*). Simultaneously, the **evidence uncertainty set** $`\mathcal{X}(E)`$ encodes all unresolved questions regarding entity boundaries, reporting periods, physical units, measurement definitions, shared third-party data sources, and suspected greenwashing claims under current diligence state $`E`$. Crucially, each element $`X \in \mathcal{X}(E)`$ specifies a *joint* input configuration across all candidate companies—preserving cross-company error dependencies rather than treating each company field as an isolated error bar. Defining the joint uncertainty space $`\Omega(E) = \mathcal{F}_\alpha \times \mathcal{X}(E)`$, we compute the exact worst-case pairwise comparison bounds for Companies $`i`$ and $`k`$: $$ \underline{\Delta}_{ik} = \inf_{(f, X) \in \Omega(E)} [f(x_i) - f(x_k)], \qquad \overline{\Delta}_{ik} = \sup_{(f, X) \in \Omega(E)} [f(x_i) - f(x_k)] $$ Whenever $`\underline{\Delta}_{ik} > 0`$, the strict ordering $`i \succ k`$ is certified across every defensible model in $`\mathcal{F}_\alpha`$ and every admissible factual resolution in $`\mathcal{X}(E)`$. If calibration establishes that $`\mathcal{X}(E)`$ contains the true ground-truth inputs with probability at least $`1 - \beta`$, a union bound guarantees joint inclusion of $`f^*`$ and the true inputs with probability at least $`1 - \alpha - \beta`$—bounding the unconditional false-certificate rate by $`\alpha + \beta`$ without assuming independence between model validation and evidence calibration. ## 3 Computing comparison bounds with support functions Our joint evidence representation also makes worst-case comparison bounds computationally tractable via **convex support functions** (*[Ben-Tal and Nemirovski](https://www2.isye.gatech.edu/~nemirovs/MOR_RCO_1998.pdf), Robust Optimization*). Let $`u \in U`$ collect shared and company-specific unresolved factual quantities (including both shared benchmark errors and company-specific greenwashing tolerances), parameterizing company inputs as $`x_i(u) = \bar{x}_i + B_i u`$. Under affine scoring models, the pairwise score difference between Company $`i`$ and Company $`k`$ takes the form $`\Delta_f(u) = m_f + a_f^\top u`$, where $`a_f = (B_i - B_k)^\top \beta_f`$. Introducing the support function $`h_U(a) = \sup_{u \in U} a^\top u`$ yields exact closed-form comparison bounds: $$ \inf_{u \in U} \Delta_f(u) = m_f - h_U(-a_f), \qquad \sup_{u \in U} \Delta_f(u) = m_f + h_U(a_f) $$ For an ellipsoidal uncertainty set $`U = \{Cz : \|z\|_2 \le r\}`$, the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality yields $`h_U(a_f) = r\|C^\top a_f\|_2`$; when $`U`$ is an $`\ell_\infty`$ box centered at zero, $`h_U(a_f)`$ reduces to a weighted sum of absolute values. This formulation delivers a major operational advantage over naive company-by-company confidence intervals: **Exact Cancellation of Shared-Source Errors**. If two companies evaluated by the same linear model share an identical additive error from a common industry benchmark or third-party sensor feed, then $`B_i = B_k`$ along those coordinates and: $$ a_f = (B_i - B_k)^\top \beta_f = 0 \implies h_U(\pm a_f) = 0 $$ The common error cancels identically in the pairwise comparison! Constructing separate uncertainty intervals for Company $`i`$ and Company $`k`$ and subtracting them falsely allows the shared source to vary in opposite directions simultaneously, manufacturing a spurious worst case that paralyzes investment decisions. Set $`m_f=\Delta_f(0)`$ and $`a_f=\nabla\Delta_f(0)`$. For smooth nonlinear models where $`\Delta_f(u)`$ is twice continuously differentiable on $`\|u\|_2 \le r`$ with Hessian operator norm bounded by $`K_f`$, Taylor's remainder theorem gives the certified lower bound: $$ |\Delta_f(u) - m_f - a_f^\top u| \le \kappa_f, \qquad \kappa_f = \frac{1}{2}K_f r^2 \implies \underline{\Delta}_f \ge m_f - r\|a_f\|_2 - \kappa_f $$ while non-smooth tree ensembles are bounded via leaf-region partitioning or mixed-integer linear programming, concentrating compute strictly on company pairs near the zero decision boundary. ## 4 Choosing verification queries by the regret they can remove When $`\underline{\Delta}_{ik} \le 0 < \overline{\Delta}_{ik}`$, the ranking between candidate investments remains unresolved—indicating that suspected greenwashing or data ambiguity could flip the decision. Rather than telling the investor which company to pick, our system recommends **which specific verification query $`q`$ (e.g., auditing a supplier contract, requesting raw utility bills, or cross-checking a regulatory filing) to execute next**. Let $`A`$ be the finite set of institutional actions (such as advancing Company $`i`$ to final diligence, advancing Company $`k`$, or deferring rating) and $`U(a, \omega)`$ be the pre-specified decision utility under scenario $`\omega \in \Omega`$. The baseline **minimax decision regret** over deterministic actions is: $$ R^*(\Omega) = \min_{a \in A} \sup_{\omega \in \Omega} \left[ \max_{b \in A} U(b, \omega) - U(a, \omega) \right] $$ Executing a verification query $`q`$ produces an observation $`o \in O_q`$ that restricts the compatible scenario set to a nonempty subset $`\Omega_{q,o} \subseteq \Omega`$. The **guaranteed worst-case reduction in decision regret** provided by query $`q`$ is: $$ V(q) = R^*(\Omega) - \sup_{o \in O_q} R^*(\Omega_{q,o}) \ge 0 $$ The non-negativity of $`V(q)`$ follows immediately from set inclusion $`\Omega_{q,o} \subseteq \Omega`$: shrinking the set of plausible greenwashing/evidence scenarios cannot increase worst-case regret for any fixed action, and minimizing over actions $`a \in A`$ preserves the inequality (*[Robust Active Preference Elicitation](https://arxiv.org/html/2003.01899)*). Crucially, **$`V(q)`$ requires no subjective probability prior over whether a corporate disclosure is exaggerated**. Under a finite diligence budget $`B`$, ranking candidate verification queries by cost-adjusted regret reduction $`V(q)/c_q`$ (or solving a small batch discrete optimization over complementary queries) directs human diligence toward shared sources and decisive claims that resolve multiple company comparisons at once. ## 5 Checking that corrections propagate through attribution Once diligence resolves a query and updates a company's verified evidence vector from $`x`$ to $`x'`$, our pipeline guarantees that the factual correction propagates deterministically through all downstream scores, peer rankings, and [SHAP](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.07874) explanations. Holding the scoring function $`f`$, background reference $`Q`$, and rubric version fixed, **Shapley efficiency** enforces the exact conservation identity (*[SHAP local accuracy property](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1705.07874)*): $$ f(x) = \phi_0 + \sum_j \phi_j(f, Q, x), \qquad \sum_j [\phi_j(f, Q, x') - \phi_j(f, Q, x)] = f(x') - f(x) $$ If approximate Shapley algorithms carry numerical summation tolerances bounded by $`\eta`$ and $`\eta'`$ before and after correction, our automated recomputation gate verifies $`|\sum_j \Delta \phi_j - \Delta f| \le \eta + \eta'`$. Every database update logs explicit version identifiers for `(Field Version, Evidence Document ID, Model Version, Background Q, Rubric Version)` so that changes driven by factual diligence corrections are never conflated with model retraining. ## 6 Reproducible quantitative comparisons Three reproducible analytical experiments verify the mathematical mechanisms derived above: 1. **Collapse of Conventional Confidence Intervals Under Shared Greenwashing / Reporting Bias**: • Set shared reporting bias $`b = 0.2`$ and independent noise $`\sigma = 1`$. Ignoring the common bias $`b`$, a nominal 95% confidence interval achieves actual coverage of only **48.40% at $`n = 100`$ records**, collapsing to **0.000637% at $`n = 1,000`$ records**. When targeted verification establishes the bias bound $`|b| \le 0.2`$, expanding the interval half-width to $`0.2 + 1.96/\sqrt{n}`$ restores **97.50% actual coverage**. 2. **Shared-Source Error Cancellation in Pairwise Company Ranking**: • Two target companies have a nominal score difference of $`0.6`$ points and share an additive sector-benchmark error in $`[-1, 1]`$. Subtracting independently constructed company intervals gives **$`[-1.4, 2.6]`$**, failing to certify an ordering. Our joint support-function model cancels the incompatible error combinations identically, yielding **$`[0.6, 0.6]`$** and certifying the ranking. 3. **Minimax-Regret Verification Routing vs. Naive [SHAP](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.07874) Attribution Ranking**: • Consider one verification query of equal cost across 8 scenarios formed from 2 Rashomon-set candidate models ($`s \in \{-1, 1\}`$) and 4 unresolved evidence configurations ($`z_1 \in \{-0.4, 0.4\}`$, $`z_2 \in \{-0.2, 0.2\}`$), with pairwise score difference $`\Delta_s = 0.15s + z_1 + 0.3s z_2`$. A further shared feature has a large [SHAP](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.07874) attribution but has already been verified ($`d_0 = 0`$). The decision action is to select Company $`i`$ or Company $`k`$, with regret measured in model-score units:
Verification QueryRemaining Regret After Worst Possible ObservationGuaranteed Reduction in Regret $`V(q)`$
**Recheck the already-resolved field with a large [SHAP](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.07874) attribution**0.61**0**
**Verify the smaller unresolved variable $`z_2`$**0.61**0**
**Verify $`z_1`$, which determines the sign of the score difference****0****0.61**
Enumerating all eight scenarios proves that ranking diligence work by raw [SHAP](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.07874) magnitude wastes 100% of the query budget ($`V(q) = 0`$), whereas our minimax-regret criterion isolates $`z_1`$ and reduces worst-case decision regret from **0.61 to zero** in a single query. By uniting **Rashomon model multiplicity**, **support-function evidence bounds**, and **minimax-regret verification routing**, this architecture provides institutional investors with a rigorous, auditable defense against AI-era greenwashing.
